name: JUSTICE HOOD
description: Concurred, holding that home rule counties must comply with state redistricting statutes and ordering the Board to draw a new map for the 2026 election.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE MÁRQUEZ
description: Concurred, argued that the relief should be granted via mandamus, not an implied private right of action, to avoid injecting confusion into mandamus jurisprudence.

name: JUSTICE HART
description: Concurred, argued that the district court lacked authority to hear the case because Scardina did not meet any of the specific statutory conditions under CADA for filing a claim in district court.

name: JUSTICE GABRIEL
description: Dissented, argued that the majority improperly decided the case on an unargued procedural ground, that the district court had jurisdiction, and Scardina had exhausted her administrative remedies, thus the merits of the case should have been addressed.

name: JUSTICE HOOD
description: Dissented, argued that the district court had jurisdiction and Scardina exhausted administrative remedies, and the merits should have been reached.

name: JUSTICE BERKENKOTTER
description: Dissented, argued that the district court had jurisdiction and Scardina exhausted administrative remedies, and the merits should have been reached.

name: JUSTICE GABRIEL
description: Concurred, argued that the Edebohls standard has been superseded and that a defendant must show both a conflict of interest and an adverse effect, unless a matter falls within limited scenarios of presumed prejudice.

name: JUSTICE MÁRQUEZ
description: Dissented, argued that Edebohls-like personal conflicts are uniquely prejudicial and should result in per se ineffective assistance of counsel, requiring automatic reversal.

name: JUSTICE HART
description: Dissented with JUSTICE MÁRQUEZ, arguing that Edebohls-like personal conflicts are uniquely prejudicial and should result in per se ineffective assistance of counsel, requiring automatic reversal.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE MÁRQUEZ
description: Concurred, argued that once a county court finds a convicted defendant poses a danger to the community, it cannot grant an appeal bond, as bail and stays of execution are separate processes, and the county court properly denied bail.

name: JUSTICE GABRIEL
description: Concurred, argued that an LWOP sentence for felony murder for an adult offender is not categorically unconstitutional and was not grossly disproportionate, even considering the 2021 reclassification, as it does not violate the Eighth Amendment or the Colorado Constitution.

name: JUSTICE GABRIEL
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court did not commit any individual errors, thus no cumulative error requiring reversal.

name: JUSTICE HOOD
description: Concurred, arguing that the supersedeas bond cap is constitutional and the trial court did not abuse its discretion regarding security and discovery.

name: JUSTICE HOOD
description: Concurred, argued that law enforcement acted in good faith when executing the reverse-keyword warrant, making the evidence admissible despite potential constitutional defects.

name: JUSTICE BERKENKOTTER
description: Concurred, argued that the search was unconstitutional due to lack of probable cause and particularity, but the evidence was admissible under the good-faith exception because law enforcement acted reasonably given the novelty of reverse-keyword searches.

name: JUSTICE MÁRQUEZ
description: Dissented, argued that the reverse-keyword warrant was unconstitutional because it lacked probable cause and particularity, functioning as an impermissible "digital dragnet," and the good-faith exception should not apply.

name: JUSTICE MÁRQUEZ
description: Concurred, argued that the CSAAA unconstitutionally creates new obligations and disabilities for past conduct by allowing time-barred claims, violating the prohibition on retrospective legislation.

name: JUSTICE GABRIEL
description: Concurred, delivered the opinion of the court.

name: JUSTICE SAMOUR
description: Concurred, argued that the legislature should review statutory provisions referencing "capital offenses" and alerted judges and lawyers to potential ramifications beyond bail.

name: SAMOUR JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that defense counsel may not call an unsubpoenaed victim present at a preliminary hearing to testify, as the Victim Rights Act (VRA) changed the legal landscape and protects victims' rights to attend without being compelled to testify without a subpoena.

name: JUSTICE HOOD
description: Concurred in the judgment, argued that the majority unnecessarily overruled McDonald and that probable cause could have been found without calling the victim, and that the VRA did not explicitly abrogate McDonald.

name: JUSTICE SAMOUR
description: Concurred, argued that a criminal defendant has a constitutionally adequate post-sentence remedy in their criminal case to seek the return of lawfully seized property, thus the CGIA's bar on civil replevin actions does not violate due process.

name: JUSTICE HART
description: Concurred, argued that the initiatives violate the single-subject requirement by combining unrelated provisions for wine sales in grocery stores and third-party alcohol delivery.

name: JUSTICE MÁRQUEZ
description: Concurred, argued that the Commission did not abuse its discretion in applying the substantive criteria of Article V, section 44.3, and that section 44.3(4)(b) does no more than incorporate existing protections against minority vote dilution as provided by the Voting Rights Act.

name: JUSTICE SAMOUR
description: Concurred, argued that Francis's ceaseless filing of meritless and often successive claims aimed at harassing opposing parties over a prolonged period of time fits the pattern for which an injunction is necessary to protect courts, litigants, and the public from abuse of the judicial process.

name: JUSTICE MÁRQUEZ
description: Concurred, argued that the General Assembly lacks authority to direct independent commissions or dictate judicial review standards, as this infringes on the independence established by voters.

name: JUSTICE HOOD
description: Dissented, argued that the General Assembly retains residual authority to legislate on matters where constitutional amendments are silent, especially to facilitate the redistricting process during unforeseen delays.

name: JUSTICE GABRIEL
description: Dissented, joining Justice Hood's opinion that the General Assembly has residual authority to legislate on matters where constitutional amendments are silent.

name: JUSTICE HART
description: Concurred, arguing that the plain language of the statute grants teachers the choice to assert portability, and therefore school districts cannot mandate waivers of nonprobationary status as a condition of employment, rendering such waivers involuntary and invalid.

name: JUSTICE SAMOUR
description: Concurred, argued that unintelligible computer sounds did not satisfy the constitutional reading requirement, but the court cannot dictate the specific manner of compliance to the legislature.

name: JUSTICE MÁRQUEZ
description: Dissented, argued that the majority failed to properly interpret Article V, Section 22, and that the bill was 'read' aloud, satisfying the constitutional requirement.

name: JUSTICE HOOD
description: Dissented, argued that the majority showed insufficient deference to the Senate's interpretation of the reading requirement and that pre-enactment injunctive relief was unwarranted.
